overview.title: Overview
overview.markdown:
indoc is a Go CLI that turns agent-written documentation and source-derived facts into a portable static site. It does not call an AI model: a coding agent writes the overview and guides, while indoc scans supported source files, extracts selected routes and environment-variable references, validates the document, and bundles the viewer.

## How it works

1. `indoc init` creates project configuration and an agent handoff guide.
2. `indoc scan --json` reports source changes, extracted reference facts, and the previous bundled narrative.
3. The coding agent writes or updates the document JSON, preserving the scanner's reference entries.
4. `indoc bundle` renders the document into static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript assets.

The result can be published as a static site or served by an existing application. `indoc serve` is only an optional localhost preview. This repository also includes a GitHub Copilot CLI skill at `.github/skills/indoc/SKILL.md`; it guides Copilot through the same scan, author, and bundle workflow.

guides.title: Install and generate your first site
guides.markdown:
## Install

Install the latest version with Go:

```sh
go install github.com/byabasaija/indoc/cmd/indoc@latest
```

Or build from a checkout with `go build -o indoc ./cmd/indoc`.

## Initialize

From the project you want to document, run:

```sh
indoc init
```

Edit `.indoc.yaml` to set the project name, source directories, and output directory. `init` also creates `.indoc/site.json`, `.indoc/site.schema.json`, and `.indoc/AGENT_GUIDE.md`.

## Generate

Ask your coding agent to read `.indoc/AGENT_GUIDE.md` and follow it. The guide directs the agent to inspect the project, run `indoc scan --json`, and author `.indoc/site.json` using the scan report's reference array unchanged. Then bundle the site:

```sh
indoc bundle --input .indoc/site.json
```

The static site is written to the configured output directory. To preview it locally, optionally run `indoc serve` and open the printed localhost URL. No preview server is needed to publish or deploy the generated files.

guides.title: Use the GitHub Copilot skill
guides.markdown:
This repository includes a project-local GitHub Copilot skill at `.github/skills/indoc/SKILL.md`. In Copilot CLI, ask:

```text
Use the /indoc skill to generate or update this repository's docs.
```

Copilot follows the skill to run the indoc workflow. If you add the skill while a Copilot CLI session is already open, reload skills with `/skills reload`; use `/skills info indoc` to inspect the loaded skill. The project skill is available when working in this repository; installing the Go CLI alone does not install it in other repositories.

guides.title: Update docs after source changes
guides.markdown:
Run a fresh scan whenever the code changes:

```sh
indoc scan --json
```

Use the report to guide the update:

- `added`, `modified`, and `deleted` identify changed source files.
- `reference` contains the current deterministic route and configuration facts. Copy this array into the document without inventing or altering entries.
- `stale_reference` identifies previous reference entries whose source files changed or were deleted; review related narrative claims too.
- `previous` contains the last bundled overview and guides to use as editable context. Verify them against the current source rather than treating them as automatically correct.

After updating `.indoc/site.json`, rebuild the static site:

```sh
indoc bundle --input .indoc/site.json
```

Commit the document JSON as the source for your generated docs. The scan cache is local state and should not be committed.

guides.title: Build and test indoc
guides.markdown:
From the repository root, run the Go test suite:

```sh
go test ./...
```

Build the CLI from source with:

```sh
go build -o indoc ./cmd/indoc
```

Use `indoc --help` to see the available commands. The main implementation areas are `internal/scanner` for incremental source hashing, `internal/reference` for deterministic fact extraction, `internal/doc` and `internal/render` for document validation and Markdown rendering, and `internal/bundler` for writing the static viewer.
